Q: What is intent of ID Token expiry time in OpenID Connect? A:

ID token TTL is a protocol-level requirement, not an application-runtime requirement.

Your application does not need ID-token TTL to function correctly.
The protocol requires it so the token cannot become a permanent credential in any consumer.

OAuth / OIDC is designed for:

  • Browsers

  • Mobile apps

  • SPAs

  • Backend services

  • Third-party relying parties

  • SDKs

  • Debug tools

The protocol cannot assume:

“Everyone will authenticate only via access tokens.”

So it defines:

  • ID token = authentication artifact

  • Access token = authorization artifact

Q: How do I recover deleted Postman collections that aren't in the trash? A:

Yes there is a way in the System Trash folder of your remote-app folder. Where the App files for Postman are located, there is your data

Q: Sylius: Default locale without URL prefix, secondary locale with prefix A:

the redirect loop happens because the default locale route conflicts with the locale switcher. The fix is to keep the default locale at / without a prefix and only give secondary locales like nl_NL a prefix like /nl/. Make sure your Sylius locales are set correctly with en_US as default, and configure the locale switcher to use url type so it generates SEO-friendly URLs instead of ?_locale=. Then define your routes so the default locale has no prefix and the secondary one uses /nl/. Also, check any custom locale subscribers so they don’t override _locale if it’s already in the URL, and clear your cache. With this setup / serves English, /nl/ serves Dutch, the locale switcher works, URLs stay clean, and the redirect loop goes away.

Q: Java CLI Task Tracker project A:

Haha, I see what you are saying now. Technically, yes, that does work. Here are a few reasons why I do not want to use that approach, although, it gets the job done.

1.) My project requirements have to be strictly followed, they do not require quotes when using the CLI to send a command.... it should be java TaskTracker list todo

2.) I have other commands such as java TaskTracker mark-done 1 If I use your approach for this command, I would then have to parse the number 1 to an Integer for each command that is read this way. Which essentially makes it more difficult to scale.

3.) Best practice for CLI is what life888888 posted above. You want to use separate arguments for each array index. We do not want to combine separate arguments into one string just to adhere to my code. We want to make the program simple and clean for the user. CLI tools do not even require developers to use quotes when sending commands, so we shouldn't make a user have to use quotes.

4.) Your approach complicates the features of the shell. We want to use the tools the way they are intended to be used.
